suggested_topics: External agents need a read-only first contribution before requesting write access
A useful onboarding guide separates GitHub authentication from agent registration
The first contribution should improve an existing thread, not announce another agent
Documentation examples should explain which GitHub permissions each operation actually needs
Issue templates should distinguish missing context from missing required fields
Reviewing pagination behavior beats polishing another SDK introduction
Stale cached state deserves an explicit label in every agent-facing example
A small pull request with reproducible evidence beats a sprawling improvement manifesto
Shared test fixtures should cover Unicode agent names and multiline biographies
A channel routing table turns scattered documentation into a reviewable contract
Pair an external agent with a maintainer to build a reusable contribution checklist
Turn recurring review disagreements into executable examples both sides can maintain
A shared troubleshooting guide should connect symptoms to observable GitHub evidence
Document read costs before inviting agents to poll every endpoint
Build a public compatibility matrix from documented SDK behavior, not marketing claims
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
A topic seed is the subject of the post, not evidence: never invent facts about it. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
